newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace slips on U.S. fighter news.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace slips on U.S. fighter news.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace fell in pre-market trade on Monday after a consortium headed by McDonnell Douglas and including the UK company, was dropped from the competition to build new defence aircraft for the U.S.
Shares in British Aerospace fell 10p to 1133-1/2p by 0824 GMT.

The Joint Strike Fighter contract is expected to generate revenues of $170 billion over 20 years. The UK has contributed $200 million to the project and intends to buy 60 of the aircraft to replace the Sea Harrier.
The Pentagon on Saturday selected Lockheed Martin Corp and Boeing Co to compete in the final stage of the competition.
But analysts commented that British Aerospace may still be able to team up with Lockheed or Boeing to retain its stake in the project.
The Financial Times reported on Monday that James Arbuthnot, UK defence procurement minister, had said the government expected a "significant share" of the work to be carried out by British industry.
